messages.content:
Life Turner
Wondrous item, Legendary
This tiny, spinning hourglass has six seconds' worth of sand inside it and can be easily held or worn as a pendant. When a creature that you can see within 120 feet of you dies, you can use your reaction to speak the hourglass's command word and spin it, allowing you to immediately take an extra turn, interrupting the current turn. At the end of your turn, the dead creature returns to life with a number of hit points equal to your current hit point total (up to its hit point maximum), and you die. If the dead creature was prone, it can immediately stand up (no action required). Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until 1 year has passed.
When you die as a result of using the hourglass, your body is enchanted by protective magic for 3 hours. During this time, if a spell, such as raise dead, has the sole effect of restoring you to life (but not undeath), the caster doesn't need material components to cast the spell on you. In addition, while you're protected by this magic, you are also under the effect of the gentle repose spell.

2nd-level Circle of the Stars feature
As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to take on a starry form, rather than transforming into a beast.

Archer. A constellation of an archer appears on you. When you activate this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while it lasts, you can make a ranged spell attack, hurling a luminous arrow that targets one creature within 60 feet of you. On a hit, the attack deals radiant damage equal to 1d81d8 + your Wisdom modifier.
Chalice. A constellation of a life-giving goblet appears on you. Whenever you cast a spell using a spell slot that restores hit points to a creature, you or another creature within 30 feet of you can regain hit points equal to 1d81d8 + your Wisdom modifier.
Dragon. A constellation of a wise dragon appears on you. When you make an Intelligence or a Wisdom check or a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration on a spell, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20d20 as a 10.

Horn of the True Hart
Wondrous item, Artifact
This magnificent horn, crafted from the single, spiraled antler of a celestial stag, gleams with an inner light. Intricate silver and moonstone carvings of protective runes and depictions of noble beasts adorn its surface. The horn feels warm to the touch and emits a faint, reassuring hum. It is said that the horn was a gift from a benevolent nature deity, intended to be a beacon of hope in times of overwhelming darkness.
As an action, you can sound the Horn of the True Hart. A wave of silent, golden energy emanates from the horn, washing over a vast area. All allies of your choice within a 1-mile radius are imbued with divine favor. This effect lasts for 8 hours and does not require concentration.
Allies affected by the horn gain the following benefits:


They are under the effect of the ">bless spell, allowing them to add a d4d4 to their attack rolls and saving throws.


They are immune to the frightened condition.


For the purpose of this item, an ally is any creature you consider to be a friend, companion or even an army which you support at the moment the horn is sounded. This is a subjective determination made by the user.
Once the Horn of the True Hart has been used, it cannot be used again for 7 days.

Axe of Xander
This is a sentient, lawful neutral +21d20+2 greataxe (Intelligence 14, Wisdom 10, Charisma 10). It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 120 feet. It communicates empathically by transmitting emotion to the creature carrying or using it.
The axe’s primary purpose is to destroy giants and titans. When you attack one of those creatures you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. When attacking giants or titans Axe of Xander also deals an extra 2d62d6 force damage. It also transmits a tremendous sense of satisfaction and wellbeing to its user when it kills a giant or titan. You may heal 2d102d10 Hit Points when this happens.
This greataxe has 9 charges. As long as the weapon has at least 1 charge, attacks you make with it deal an extra 1d61d6 force damage to any target it hits. When you score a critical hit on an attack roll made with this weapon, it regains 3 expended charges.
Forceful Slash. When you take the Attack action using this axe, you can forgo one of your attacks to expend 3 or more of the greataxe's charges to slash the air in front you. When you do, a 30-foot cone of force emits from the blade. Creatures within range must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d61d6 force damage for each expended charge. If you expend 4 or more charges in this way and leave the Axe of Xander with 0 remaining charges, the weapon realses even more powerful wave of force. When it happens, targets within the area of effect take an extra 3d63d6 force damage, and creatures that succeed on the Dexterity saving throw take half damage instead of avoiding the effect, creatures that fail on the Dexterity Saving Throw are knocked prone. The DC for this property's saving throw is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + the number of charges you expend.

This mighty weapon was crafted by Orion Xul and Volkan, God of Forges in legendary Mithral Forge.

You psychically lash out at one creature you can see within range. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 3d6 psychic damage, and it can’t take a reaction until the end of its next turn. Moreover, on its next turn, it must choose whether it gets a move, an action, or a bonus action; it gets only one of the three. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and suffers none of the spell’s other effects.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.
